function.mechanism: A synthetic azo chromophore system absorbs visible light to impart dark blue-black/purple colour in foods.
common_food_categories: processed foods requiring dark colour standardization

adi.basis: EFSA 2010 re-evaluation retained ADI 5 mg/kg bw/day; 2015 refined exposure update followed this ADI framework.

efsa.key_finding: EFSA retained ADI 5 mg/kg bw/day; intake was generally below ADI but high-percentile child exposure could exceed ADI in upper-end scenarios.

fda.cfr_citation: 21 CFR 70.3(j); 21 CFR 70.5; 21 CFR Part 73 Subpart A; 21 CFR Part 74 Subpart A

adi.basis: JECFA ADI 0-1 mg/kg bw; 2019 entry states no reason to revise previously established ADI.

concerns.summary: A 2004 study reported positive micronucleus/Comet assay findings for Brilliant Black BN in tested systems; EFSA also discussed in vitro positive micronucleus/Comet findings in its 2010 re-evaluation context.
Brilliant Black BN showed receptor-level allosteric pharmacology in vitro (adenosine A1/A3 receptor study), indicating biological activity but not establishing chronic dietary harm.

no_concern_confirmed: EFSA 2010 concluded no reason to revise ADI and noted long-term carcinogenicity studies were negative.
JECFA 2019 concluded newly available information did not warrant revising ADI 0-1 mg/kg bw.

populations: toddlers and children in upper-end refined exposure scenarios
adi_exceedance.notes: EFSA 2010 reported a child 95th-percentile estimate above ADI (6.9 mg/kg bw/day) while mean intakes were generally below ADI.

risk_assessment.rationale: E151 has established ADIs and ongoing regulatory acceptance, but upper-end child exposure scenarios and persistent genotoxicity/mechanistic discussion prevent classifying it as clearly low concern across all intake strata.
key_factors: EFSA ADI retained at 5 mg/kg bw/day
JECFA ADI retained at 0-1 mg/kg bw (latest evaluation year 2019)
High-percentile child exposure can exceed ADI in EFSA scenarios
In vitro genotoxic signals reported in published literature
No IARC monograph classification identified for E151
